pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql: NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' asserts existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item(); test 'AC-2' checks '— high', '— low' and no label on normal.
WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id; test 'AC-3' checks high, low and normal filters in id order.
Unfiltered query ORDER BY id; test 'AC-4' checks full list in order.
nav() renders All/High/Normal/Low with the current one in <strong>; test 'AC-5' checks exact nav HTML for all four views.
Returns 400 when the priority param is present and not in the set, including an empty value; test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks no <li>.
The COUNT query picks 'No X-priority items.' only when the table is non-empty; test 'AC-7' covers high, low and normal no-match plus empty table in all four views.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; the checker regex now permits a query; test 'AC-8' asserts it, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers it.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and decisions. Existing items default to normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the traffic-checker query allowance, which AC-8 requires.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and named by tests. All 4 state-table rows have tests. The spec was added in the change as one commit, with no later edits to it.

vitest isn't installed here, so I couldn't run the tests; CI covers that. By reading, the tests assert exact HTML and lists, and each test starts from a fresh DB with migrations applied. The fakeApp change in test/traffic.test.js is additive, and no tests were deleted.
The README describes the filter and the new route is listed. No stale docs found.
Parameterised SQL with a whitelist. The empty-string and prototype-key values are handled. The extra COUNT query is needed to tell 'No items yet.' from a no-match filter.
The priority value is whitelisted and bound as a parameter; titles are still escaped. No injected instructions found in the repository content.
A minimal server-rendered HTML page with no styling, and the diff touches no UI files such as CSS or templates. Nav semantics are covered under the AC-5 tests.
No browser flow in the diff beyond plain links; the core flow is covered by HTTP-level tests.
The title and body match the diff. The claims about the traffic checker, the fake app and the tests are true.
